stem: Two towns are 270 km apart. A bus leaves one town at 50 km/h, and at the same time a car leaves the other town at 40 km/h. They drive toward each other. After how many hours will they meet?
hints: When they move toward each other, the gap between them shrinks by both distances each hour.
Each hour the gap gets 50 + 40 = 90 km smaller.

steps.action: Let t = the hours until they meet.
In t hours, the bus goes 50 × t km and the car goes 40 × t km.
steps.why: Distance = rate × time for each vehicle.

steps.action: Together they cover the whole 270 km: 50t + 40t = 270.

steps.why: 90 km/h is their combined speed. The gap shrinks by 90 km every hour.

steps.action: Divide both sides by 90: t = 270 ÷ 90 = 3 hours.
Check: the bus goes 50 × 3 = 150 km and the car goes 40 × 3 = 120 km. 150 + 120 = 270 km. They meet after 3 hours.

trapNotes.6: This divides by 45, the average of the two speeds. Each hour the gap shrinks by 50 + 40 = 90 km, not 45 km.
trapNotes.27: This subtracts the speeds: 270 ÷ (50 − 40). Subtract speeds only when vehicles go the same direction. Toward each other, add them.
trapNotes.1/3: This is 90 ÷ 270, upside down. Time = distance ÷ speed: 270 ÷ 90.
